verdicts.reason: Both blow the small footer wordmark up into a huge header logo that becomes the focal point and drowns out the quote, so the hierarchy and brand proportion are wrong. A at least anchors the quote mark, quote and attribution to a shared left margin and keeps the can a good size, though its logo floats at an arbitrary off-centre x and the quote is undersized. B centres the logo but starts the text block at an arbitrary x≈180, leaving dead space on the left; its quote's line end runs into the purple circle and the can shrinks to a minor element.
